clue.text: Law passed by House after a complaint put in motion

indicators.note: setting the words in motion stirs them up, so the letters of after a complaint are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grumble from the public leads Parliament to pass a new statute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in motion' looks like parliamentary procedure (a motion in the House) but it signals the anagram of AFTER A COMPLAINT.
explanation.definitionFit: A statute passed by Parliament (House) is the formal name for a law enacted there.

clue.text: Drawn from every part of university left

parts.note: all means the whole, every part
red is used for left-wing, socialist politics

explanation.surface: Someone is taken from every corner of a university with left-wing leanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To be enticed or attracted is to be drawn in, tempted.

clue.text: As if Chicken and Rice perhaps should be put on in a lazy way

indicators.note: the first name is placed on top of the other piece, as this is a down clue

parts.note: Tim Rice is the lyricist, so Rice suggests the first name Tim
idly means lazily

explanation.surface: A recipe note: chicken and rice, cooked lazily.
explanation.walkthrough: Chicken and Rice look like a dish but are a coward and the lyricist Tim Rice.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting like a chicken means acting like a coward, fearfully and nervously.

clue.text: Defence Secretary's promise holding individuals to resign

indicators.note: the possessive name grips the other piece inside it

parts.note: Michael Fallon was the UK Defence Secretary; the possessive gives FALLON plus S
ones are single units or individuals
a word is a promise, as in giving one's word

explanation.surface: A minister's pledge to keep certain people, then quit.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Fallon did resign as Defence Secretary in 2017, which makes the surface apt.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom, from a defeated Roman general's suicide, means to quit honourably after failure.

clue.text: Church person, a product of Lancing

indicators.note: a product is something made from material, so the letters of Lancing are reworked

explanation.surface: A churchgoer educated at Lancing, an English private school.
explanation.walkthrough: Lancing College is a public school in Sussex with a Church of England foundation.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Church of England or a related communion is described this way.

clue.text: Cream shut up, cat being around

indicators.note: the cat surrounds the other piece

parts.note: a lion is a big cat

indicators.note: in a down clue the word for shut is read upwards, back to front

parts.note: to describes a door pushed shut, as in pull the door to

explanation.surface: Someone told to keep quiet while a cat prowls near some cream.
explanation.definitionFit: A cream or liquid preparation applied to the skin is this kind of product.

clue.text: That poor fathead beaten up without provocation

indicators.note: the words are beaten up and mangled, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A poor fool gets thumped for no reason at all.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means readily, at the slightest excuse, without needing to be provoked.

clue.text: Ban thus restricts business expert

indicators.note: the word for thus confines the expert inside it

parts.note: ergo is Latin for therefore, thus
an MBA is a Master of Business Administration

explanation.surface: A ban therefore limits what a consultant can do.
explanation.definitionFit: An official prohibition on trade with a country is a ban.

clue.text: Over-sentimentality of Electra complex

indicators.note: complex means intricate or tangled, so the letters of Electra are jumbled

explanation.surface: Freudian theory: the Electra complex is mere mawkishness.
explanation.walkthrough: The Electra complex is a psychology term; 'complex' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloying sweetness of sentiment is likened to the sticky syrup, a figurative sense.

clue.text: It illuminates difficulty following strike

indicators.note: the word for difficulty comes after the word for strike

parts.note: to lam is to hit or thrash
a plight is a predicament or difficulty

explanation.surface: Something lights up a problem that arises after industrial action.
explanation.definitionFit: Light from a lamp is what shows things up, so it is something that illuminates.

clue.text: Information presented systematically in small computer incomplete

indicators.note: the word for the small computer is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a tablet is a small handheld computer

explanation.surface: Data is laid out neatly on a little computer, but not all of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A grid of rows and columns is the standard way to set out information systematically.

clue.text: Set a date, initially in South American city

indicators.note: the A and the letter from date go inside the name of the city

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro, usually just Rio, is in Brazil

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word date is taken

explanation.surface: Arranging a date in Rio, or so it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: A set is a receiving apparatus, as in a wireless or television set, so a broadcast receiver.

clue.text: One certain knack that's reduced kind of exercise

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
some means certain, as in some people

indicators.note: the word for knack is shortened by dropping its final letter

parts.note: a trick is a knack, as in the trick of it

explanation.surface: A single sure technique, slimmed down, as a form of workout.
explanation.definitionFit: Exercise where muscles contract against resistance without the joint moving is called this type.

clue.text: A toddy drunk certainly makes you regular

indicators.note: a drink that is drunk is jumbled, so the letters of a toddy are rearranged

parts.note: ay is an old or dialect yes, meaning certainly

explanation.surface: A nightly hot toddy keeps you regular, the clue says with a wink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' reshuffles A TODDY into DAYTOD; AY (yes) completes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something everyday and routine happens as a matter of ordinary course, so regular.

clue.text: Shaw comes across old and hollow?

indicators.note: the word for the wood spans the letter for old, holding it inside

parts.note: a shaw is an old word for a small wood or thicket

explanation.surface: George Bernard Shaw meets an old man and finds him empty.
explanation.walkthrough: Shaw looks like the playwright but is the dialect word for a copse.
explanation.definitionFit: A long narrow channel or furrow is a hollow cut into a surface.

clue.text: Flourish taking healthy food recipe

parts.note: bran is fibre-rich husk eaten for health
a dish is a prepared recipe or meal

explanation.surface: Thriving thanks to wholesome cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: To flourish a sword is to wave it about, so the verb fits as a synonym.

clue.text: River creature found by water rat

parts.note: R is the usual map abbreviation for river
an otter is an animal living by rivers and streams

explanation.surface: A riverbank animal is spotted next to a water rat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'water rat' reads as one animal, but 'rat' alone is the definition, a scoundrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A rat is a contemptible or treacherous person, and a cad or scoundrel is the same.

clue.text: Spots beautiful Italian female following Rugby

indicators.note: the Italian word comes after the abbreviation for rugby

parts.note: RU stands for Rugby Union
bella is Italian for beautiful, in the feminine

explanation.surface: Someone spots a lovely Italian woman after a rugby match.
explanation.definitionFit: German measles is an infection known for producing a rash of red spots.

clue.text: After time, Swallows and Amazons author almost makes one beam

indicators.note: the author's name comes after the letter for time
the author's surname loses its final letter

parts.note: Arthur Ransome wrote the children's book Swallows and Amazons

explanation.surface: A children's author seems to be adding up a single sum after hours.
explanation.definitionFit: A horizontal crossbar above a door or window is a structural beam.

clue.text: Fat duke excellent in old-fashioned way

parts.note: ripping is dated British slang for splendid

explanation.surface: A plump aristocrat is described as first-rate in a dated manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Fat that has melted from roasting meat is collected and used in cooking.

clue.text: Legion assembled around British base

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round the abbreviation
assembled means put together, so the letters of legion are arranged anew

explanation.surface: A legion gathers around a British military base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assembled' makes IGNOLE from LEGION, and 'around' puts B inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Base, in the sense of low and dishonourable, is a synonym for dishonourable conduct.

clue.text: Pet overturned animal 'ouse — share the cost

indicators.note: in a down clue the word for pet is turned upside down

parts.note: a dog is a pet
a hutch is a house for a rabbit; dropping its H, as the apostrophe in 'ouse shows, leaves the rest

explanation.surface: A rabbit hutch is knocked over, and its cost split.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'ouse mimics a Cockney dropped H, telling you to drop the H of hutch.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means each pays their own way, splitting the bill evenly.

clue.text: What one gets to change the locks

definitions.text: What one gets to change the locks

parts.words: What one gets to change the locks
parts.note: locks here are tresses of hair, not door fastenings, so this is a visit to the hairdresser

explanation.surface: A security upgrade after a break-in.
explanation.definitionFit: A new style of the tresses is what a salon visit produces.

clue.text: Was I not AB at sea? Yes I was

definitions.text: Was I not AB at sea? Yes I was

indicators.note: being at sea means confused, so the letters of was I not AB are scrambled

explanation.surface: A senior sailor insists he served as an ordinary seaman once.
explanation.walkthrough: AB is an able seaman; a ship's petty officer typically rises from that rank, hence 'Yes I was'.
explanation.definitionFit: The petty officer in charge of rigging and deck crew was once an able seaman himself.

clue.text: Trendy arrested by FBI agent and given punishment

indicators.note: the word for trendy is held inside the word for the agent

parts.note: a fed is American slang for a federal agent
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: A fashionable person is picked up by the FBI and penalised.
explanation.definitionFit: Being made to pay money as a penalty is a common form of punishment.

clue.text: What one may throw and see snaring beast of burden

indicators.note: the word for see traps the beast within it

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold
an ass or donkey carries loads

explanation.surface: A cowboy hurls something and watches it catch a donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: A rope with a running noose is something cowboys hurl to catch cattle.

clue.text: Once more live in check clothes

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain
a habit is a garment, such as a nun's or a riding habit

explanation.surface: Someone moves back home and inspects their wardrobe.
explanation.definitionFit: Occupying a dwelling again is to inhabit it a second time.

clue.text: Having many weapons thereto met death in action

indicators.note: the letters are set into action, moving about into a new order

explanation.surface: A soldier met his end in battle, rather archaically.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone heavily equipped with arms, fully weaponed.
